sections.h2: How do you contact the Brunswick County Tax Office?
sections.html:
One office in the David R. Sandifer Administration Building, 30 Government Center Drive, Bolivia, NC 28422, does appraisal, assessment, ownership records and tax collection. Its main number is 910-253-2829. For relief programs, call 910-253-2811 on weekdays between 8:30 a.m. and 5 p.m.

From the tax office page on the county website you reach tax bills, property record cards, certifications, the foreclosure list and land records. A payment plan through the collections division is available for owners who cannot clear a bill in one payment; ask before the balance is late.

sections.h2: What do Brunswick County's housing numbers mean for a seller?
sections.html:
Brunswick County has grown fast. The Census Bureau estimates 174,702 people in July 2025, up 27.8% from 136,695 in the April 2020 base, on 850.08 square miles of land.

QuickFacts lists 116,023 housing units, with 84.6% owner-occupied by the Census rate. The 2020 to 2024 median value is $349,800, and the median gross rent is $1,351. People 65 and older make up 36.6% of residents. Builders took out 4,457 permits in 2025, and each new house or addition can change a parcel's value ahead of the next reappraisal.

The rate schedule names 19 towns and villages, among them Bolivia, Northwest, Leland, Navassa, Shallotte, Southport, Oak Island, Holden Beach, Ocean Isle Beach, Sunset Beach, Caswell Beach and Bald Head Island. The town where a parcel sits determines which town rate gets added to the county rate.

sections.h2: What is the Brunswick County property tax rate?
sections.html:
Brunswick levies 0.3420, which is 34.20 cents per $100 of value, and the county schedule shows that rate unchanged for 2024, 2025 and 2026. In 2022 the rate was 0.485, and it dropped to 0.342 in 2023, the year of the last countywide revaluation.

sections.h2: How will the 2027 Brunswick County revaluation and appeal process work?
sections.html:
All real property will be valued as of January 1, 2027, at its market value and condition on that date. Anything still under construction is appraised by its percentage of completion.

Notices of the new value are scheduled for February and March 2027. Check your notice against the record card for errors in the property data. Appeals then run in two stages:

  • Informal review: from January until the board of equalization and review convenes, the tax assessor can adjust a value when the facts support it.
  • Formal appeal: after the board convenes, it holds the authority, and owners or their representatives normally present their case in person.

An appeal received after the board convenes is handled as formal. One that arrives after adjournment is untimely and generally waits for the next year, and a successful appeal is not retroactive to earlier years. The board's first meeting falls from the first Monday in April to the first Monday in May under G.S. 105-322, and in a reappraisal year it must finish by December 1. The next step up, the Property Tax Commission, takes appeals filed within 30 days of the board's mailed decision.

sections.h2: What is the payment calendar for a Brunswick County tax bill?
sections.html:
September 1 is the due date. Interest holds off through January 5, or the next business day when January 5 lands on a weekend. The county mailed 2026 bills in mid-August, and they can be paid without interest through January 5, 2027.

After that, state law starts the clock: 2% from January 6 to February 1, then three-fourths of a percent for every month or part of a month until paid. Mail counts as paid on the postmark date. A county or town may adopt a prepayment discount by a resolution passed by May 1, so ask the tax office if one is on offer.

The county's claim for the tax runs from the January 1 listing date and can be enforced by suing in foreclosure.

sections.h2: What relief can a Brunswick County owner apply for?
sections.html:
The county's relief page lists four programs. The elderly or disabled exclusion takes off the greater of $25,000 or 50% of appraised value on a permanent residence for an owner who is 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, with income under the limit. NCDOR lists $38,800 for 2026.

  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value comes off, with no age or income condition. A surviving spouse who has not remarried can claim it.
  • Homestead circuit breaker: annual tax is capped at 4% of income, or 5% for income above the limit but within 150% of it, and the excess is deferred as a lien.
  • Present-use value: qualifying farm, horticultural or forest land is assessed on its use value, not its market value.

On the county's page, deferred circuit breaker taxes for the three latest years become due with interest if the owner dies, transfers the property, or stops living there. A sale therefore brings the bill. File on the state form with the county tax office in the January listing period, noting that the county must accept filings through June 1.

sections.h2: How do taxes affect a Brunswick County house sale?
sections.html:
Brunswick County requires, by resolution, that a deed be stamped by the tax office before the Register of Deeds will record it. The stamp shows that taxes, fees and assessments are paid.

To see what is owed, an owner, attorney or other interested party can request a Tax Certification under G.S. 105-361. It reports local tax liens, deferred taxes where they exist, fire fees and assessments that the office must collect. Ask for it early, since deferred circuit breaker or present-use taxes show up on it.

The seller also pays the state deed tax of $1.00 per $500 of consideration to the Register of Deeds ahead of recording.

Properties with unpaid taxes can go to a county auction on the steps of the courthouse in Bolivia, rain or shine. Winning bidders pay a 5% deposit on the spot in cash, certified or cashier's check or money order, and the county provides no financing. A 10-day upset period follows, and each higher bid must beat the last by 5% or $750, whichever is more. The winner has a week after notice to pay the rest and receives a commissioner's deed. A homeowner can still sell and pay the taxes at closing while the process is pending.

faqs.q: Who do I call at the Brunswick County Tax Office?
faqs.a: Call 910-253-2829 for the Tax Office or 910-253-2811 for relief programs. The office is at 30 Government Center Drive in Bolivia.

faqs.q: What is the county tax rate in Brunswick County?
faqs.a: The county rate is 0.3420 for 2024, 2025 and 2026, with town or district rates added where they apply.

faqs.q: What date does the next Brunswick County revaluation take effect?
faqs.a: January 1, 2027, with notices scheduled between February and March 2027. The prior revaluation was effective January 1, 2023.

faqs.q: Does Brunswick County give a grace period on late tax bills?
faqs.a: Not after January 5. Interest begins the next day, and the collections division can arrange a payment plan if you call before the deadline.

faqs.q: Does Brunswick County make sellers get a tax stamp before recording?
faqs.a: Yes. By county resolution the tax office must stamp a deed before the Register of Deeds records it, which confirms taxes, fees and assessments are settled.
